name: llama-server
summary: A llama.cpp server on this machine (or reached through an SSH tunnel), no key: chat completions and a health check

connect.description: A llama.cpp server on this machine, no key (http, loopback)

notes: Pass your own port: lotr add-http NAME@zone --from-template llama-server --base-url http://127.0.0.1:PORT. llama-server's own default is 9931; gt's farm engines use 8080, which is this template's default.

A server on another machine: LOTR refuses plain http to anything but this machine, so reach it through an SSH tunnel to loopback: ssh -N -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 user@host (keep it running, or use autossh or a launchd job), then register http://127.0.0.1:8080.
Nothing here is authenticated: llama-server has no key unless it was started with --api-key. Keep it on a trusted network and never put a secret in a prompt sent to it.
lotr status --check asks GET /health: ok means the model is loaded; a 503 means it is still loading.
Whether a packet fits the engine's usable context is the farm's decision (gt-farm keeps its own calibration), not this template's.
